_note: Evergreen idea prompts per lane, written for docs/voice.md (calm, honest, dry). Trading = his own process and psychology only: no tickers, no setups, no buy/sell, no return claims. No places. Keys are stable: they become ideas.source_key 'niche-<lane>-<key>', so never rename one.

gym.title: The warm-up I never skip
gym.hook: The most boring five minutes of my session are the reason the rest of it works.
gym.about: Your actual warm-up, start to finish, and why it stayed.
gym.adapt: Film the warm-up once, say each step in a few words, end on the first working set.

gym.title: What a missed week actually cost me
gym.hook: I missed a full week of training and the scary part wasn't the strength.
gym.about: Honest look at coming back after time off: what dropped, what didn't.
gym.adapt: Only say what you really noticed. If nothing dropped, say that.

gym.title: Slowing the negative down
gym.hook: I took weight off the bar and the set got harder.
gym.about: Tempo work: why lighter and slower humbled you.
gym.adapt: Show one set at your normal tempo and one slowed down, side by side.

gym.title: My own form check, unflattering
gym.hook: I filmed my squat from the side for the first time and I have notes.
gym.about: Self-review of a lift from a new angle, one fix you made.
gym.adapt: Point out one real flaw, then show the corrected rep. Self-roast is fine.

gym.title: Why I deload before I want to
gym.hook: The week I least want to deload is usually the week I need it most.
gym.about: How you decide a lighter week is due, from your own signals.
gym.adapt: Name the two or three signs you actually go by, nothing borrowed.

gym.title: Timing my rest for a week
gym.hook: I timed my rest between sets for a week and I was lying to myself.
gym.about: What you found when you measured rest instead of guessing.
gym.adapt: Only use the real gap you saw. No timer data, no number.

gym.title: Running the same program longer than feels fun
gym.hook: The program didn't stop working, I just got bored of it.
gym.about: Consistency over novelty, from your own training block.
gym.adapt: Say how many weeks you've really run it and what you'd change, if anything.

gym.title: Sleep versus my top set
gym.hook: My best lifts this month all came after the nights I went to bed on time.
gym.about: Recovery basics shown through your own week, not a lecture.
gym.adapt: Keep it to your own pattern; don't claim it works the same for everyone.

gym.title: Small plates, small wins
gym.hook: Adding two and a half pounds a week sounds slow until you do it for a semester.
gym.about: Micro-progression and why patience beats big jumps.
gym.adapt: Use your real starting and current weight only if you have them; otherwise keep it general.

gym.title: The set where ego took over
gym.hook: Every bad rep I've done had the same cause, and it wasn't the weight.
gym.about: A dry self-roast about chasing a number in front of nobody.
gym.adapt: Tell it as one short story, end on what you do differently now.

gym.title: One thing physical therapy taught me about lifting
gym.hook: The most useful lifting advice I've had came from someone who never mentioned weight.
gym.about: A recovery or mobility lesson you actually apply.
gym.adapt: One lesson, one demo, plain words. No medical claims.

gym.title: Feeling the muscle versus moving the weight
gym.hook: I moved the weight for years before I actually felt the muscle working.
gym.about: A cue that changed a lift for you.
gym.adapt: Show the cue on one exercise, say it in one sentence.

gym.title: Training on a bad day
gym.hook: Some days the win is just showing up and doing the warm-up sets.
gym.about: What a low-energy session looks like for you, honestly.
gym.adapt: Film a real low-energy day; don't dress it up.

gym.title: Why I stopped checking the mirror daily
gym.hook: Looking every day made it look like nothing was changing.
gym.about: Tracking progress without obsessing, from your own habits.
gym.adapt: Say how often you check now and why. No body comparisons with others.

gym.title: The one exercise I'd keep
gym.hook: If I could only keep one exercise, it wouldn't be the one you think.
gym.about: Your pick and the honest reason.
gym.adapt: Pick one you really do weekly, show a set, one line on why.

gym.title: Being new in the weight room
gym.hook: Nobody in the gym is watching you as closely as you think.
gym.about: Calm reassurance for newer lifters from your own first months.
gym.adapt: Tell one real early moment, keep it light, no lecture.

gym.title: Why I write every set down
gym.hook: My training got better the week I started writing everything down.
gym.about: Logging as the simplest progress tool.
gym.adapt: Show your actual log for a few seconds, no other people's names in it.

gym.title: When the grip goes first
gym.hook: My back was ready for more, my hands weren't.
gym.about: A weak link you found and how you trained it.
gym.adapt: Only the fix you really used, one or two lines.

gym.title: Making peace with cardio
gym.hook: I avoided cardio for a year because I thought it would kill my gains. It didn't.
gym.about: Your honest take on running alongside lifting.
gym.adapt: Your own experience only; no claims about what it does for everyone.

gym.title: Three sessions a week, every week
gym.hook: Three average sessions a week beat five perfect ones I never finish.
gym.about: Consistency over intensity, shown with your real schedule shape.
gym.adapt: Don't name days or times you train; keep it to how many and how it feels.

gym.title: The pump is not progress
gym.hook: The pump feels like progress and it mostly isn't.
gym.about: Dry take on what you actually track instead.
gym.adapt: Say what you track, keep the self-roast gentle.

gym.title: Resetting between reps
gym.hook: The rep I rush is always the rep that looks worst on camera.
gym.about: Why you pause and reset on heavy sets.
gym.adapt: Show one rushed rep and one reset rep.

gym.title: The accessory work nobody films
gym.hook: The exercises that fixed my lifts are the ones I'd never post.
gym.about: Unglamorous accessories that carry the main lifts.
gym.adapt: Show two of them quickly, one line each on why.

gym.title: Fitting training around classes
gym.hook: The best training plan is the one that survives a full week of classes.
gym.about: How you keep training going in a busy semester, without naming your school.
gym.adapt: Keep it general: 'college', 'classes'. Never which one, never when.

gym.title: Sore doesn't mean it worked
gym.hook: I used to judge a workout by how sore I was the next day.
gym.about: A common belief you dropped.
gym.adapt: One short story, what you go by now.

gym.title: What a PR day actually looks like
gym.hook: My last PR looked exactly like a normal Tuesday, and that's the point.
gym.about: The unglamorous build-up behind a personal best.
gym.adapt: Only a PR you really hit; the number only if you want to share it.

gym.title: Rest days without guilt
gym.hook: Taking the rest day is the part of the program I'm worst at.
gym.about: Recovery as part of the plan, said honestly.
gym.adapt: Say what you actually do on rest days, keep it calm.

gym.title: What I'd tell myself in year one
gym.hook: If I could redo my first year of lifting, I'd change almost nothing about the exercises.
gym.about: The real first-year mistakes were habits, not programs.
gym.adapt: Pick one habit you'd change, not a list of ten.

gym.title: Bracing finally clicked
gym.hook: I lifted for a year before anyone showed me how to breathe under the bar.
gym.about: A form basic that changed your heavy sets.
gym.adapt: Explain the cue in one sentence, show one rep. No medical claims.

gym.title: A completely average training week
gym.hook: Nothing happened in the gym this week, and I think that's what progress looks like.
gym.about: Consistency shown through a deliberately unremarkable week.
gym.adapt: Quick cuts of normal sessions, a dry closing line.

trading.title: Writing my rules before the open
trading.hook: The only version of me I trust with my rules is the one before the market opens.
trading.about: Why you decide exits and limits before anything is on the line.
trading.adapt: Show the habit, not the rules themselves if they're setups. Not financial advice.

trading.title: The hardest trade is not taking one
trading.hook: Some of my best sessions had zero trades in them.
trading.about: Sitting out as a skill, from your own journal.
trading.adapt: Talk about the decision, never about what price did after.

trading.title: What my trade journal actually looks like
trading.hook: My journal has more lines about how I felt than about price.
trading.about: Journaling emotions and decisions, not just outcomes.
trading.adapt: Blur anything that shows a setup or a number. Focus on the habit.

trading.title: Recognising revenge trading
trading.hook: I can tell I'm about to revenge trade because I start typing faster.
trading.about: Your own early warning signs after a loss.
trading.adapt: Name your real signs, end on what you do when you notice them.

trading.title: A red day I'm proud of
trading.hook: I lost money today and it was one of my better days.
trading.about: Grading the process instead of the result.
trading.adapt: No amounts. Say which rule you followed and why it mattered.

trading.title: A green day I'm not proud of
trading.hook: Getting paid for a bad decision is the most expensive thing that can happen to me.
trading.about: Why a lucky win can reinforce a bad habit.
trading.adapt: Keep it about the decision; no numbers, no setup.

trading.title: Less screen time, better decisions
trading.hook: The longer I stare at the chart, the worse my decisions get.
trading.about: Limiting screen time as part of your process.
trading.adapt: Your own rule for when you close the screen; don't name times tied to where you are.

trading.title: Sizing down when I'm not sure
trading.hook: When I'm unsure, I don't skip the plan, I make it smaller.
trading.about: Risk as a feeling you manage, not a number to brag about.
trading.adapt: Talk about the principle only. No sizes, no instruments. Not financial advice.

trading.title: What FOMO feels like from the inside
trading.hook: FOMO doesn't feel like greed, it feels like being sure.
trading.about: Naming the feeling so you can catch it.
trading.adapt: One real moment, told calmly, no outcome numbers.

trading.title: Boring trading is good trading
trading.hook: If a session feels exciting, I've probably already broken something.
trading.about: Calm as a signal of a working process.
trading.adapt: Say how you check yourself when it gets exciting.

trading.title: My most repeated mistake
trading.hook: I've made the same trading mistake more times than I'd like to admit.
trading.about: Honest self-roast about a habit you're still fixing.
trading.adapt: Name the habit, not a setup. Say what you're trying now.

trading.title: Sleep and my decisions
trading.hook: My worst trading days line up suspiciously well with my worst nights of sleep.
trading.about: Recovery matters for focus, not just for lifting.
trading.adapt: Your own pattern only; no claims for everyone.

trading.title: What the gym taught me about trading
trading.hook: Lifting taught me to follow a plan when I don't feel like it, and trading tests that every day.
trading.about: Discipline carrying over between the two lanes.
trading.adapt: One clear parallel from your own week.

trading.title: Not checking a closed trade
trading.hook: Once a trade is closed, looking at what happened next only teaches me regret.
trading.about: Letting go of what-ifs as a process rule.
trading.adapt: Say why you stopped, keep it short.

trading.title: Where I am in the learning curve
trading.hook: I'm not a profitable trader yet, and I'm fine saying that out loud.
trading.about: Honest status update on your own learning, no claims.
trading.adapt: Say what you're working on this month. Never a number you don't have.

trading.title: My prep routine, minus the setups
trading.hook: Most of my trading happens before I place anything.
trading.about: The non-chart parts of preparing: sleep, notes, mindset.
trading.adapt: Show the routine, keep charts out of frame. Not financial advice.

trading.title: The rule I break most
trading.hook: I have one rule I break more than all the others combined.
trading.about: Self-honesty about where your discipline leaks.
trading.adapt: Name the type of rule (time, size, patience), not a setup.

trading.title: Patience is a position
trading.hook: Waiting is the part of trading nobody posts, and it's most of the job.
trading.about: Patience as the main skill, from your own sessions.
trading.adapt: Calm voiceover over a quiet desk shot.

trading.title: Being okay with being wrong
trading.hook: The faster I admit I'm wrong, the cheaper it is.
trading.about: Ego versus process when a trade goes against you.
trading.adapt: Tell it as how you think about it now, no amounts.

trading.title: Muting trading social media
trading.hook: My trading got calmer the week I muted every trading account I followed.
trading.about: Protecting focus from other people's results.
trading.adapt: Don't name or mock anyone. Just what changed for you.

trading.title: What my first month of trading taught me
trading.hook: My first month of trading taught me more about myself than about markets.
trading.about: Early psychology lessons from your own start.
trading.adapt: One or two lessons, plain, no results.

trading.title: Scoring my day by process
trading.hook: I give every trading day a score, and money isn't part of it.
trading.about: A simple process scorecard you actually use.
trading.adapt: Show the categories, not the trades.

trading.title: When I call it a day
trading.hook: I have a rule for when I'm done for the day, and it has nothing to do with the chart.
trading.about: Stopping rules based on your state, not price.
trading.adapt: Say the kind of rule, keep specifics general.

trading.title: Small and consistent
trading.hook: I'd rather be boringly consistent than occasionally brilliant.
trading.about: Why steady habits matter more than big days.
trading.adapt: Your own reasoning, no outcomes.

trading.title: Losses are tuition, but only if I take notes
trading.hook: A loss is only tuition if I actually write down what it taught me.
trading.about: Turning losses into notes instead of feelings.
trading.adapt: Show the journal habit, blur numbers.

trading.title: Feeling it is normal
trading.hook: I still feel every loss, I just don't let it make the next decision.
trading.about: Separating feeling from acting.
trading.adapt: Calm, one idea, close on the separation.

trading.title: Breaks between sessions
trading.hook: Getting up from the desk is the most underrated part of my process.
trading.about: Physical resets as a trading habit.
trading.adapt: Short clip of the reset, no times or places.

trading.title: Why I share the bad days
trading.hook: I post my bad trading days because the good ones teach me less.
trading.about: Honesty as part of your journal.
trading.adapt: Say it calmly, no numbers needed. Not financial advice.

trading.title: No shortcuts I've found
trading.hook: Every shortcut I tried in trading turned out to be a longer way around.
trading.about: Skepticism about quick fixes, from your own experience.
trading.adapt: Don't name products or people. Your experience only.

trading.title: Good decision, bad outcome
trading.hook: I made the right call today and it still didn't work, and that's fine.
trading.about: Decision quality versus outcome, applied to a real day.
trading.adapt: Talk about the reasoning, never the trade details.

other.title: Balancing college, training and everything else
other.hook: My schedule isn't balanced, it just rotates what I'm neglecting.
other.about: An honest look at juggling classes, training and trading.
other.adapt: Keep it general: 'classes', 'college'. Never which one or when.

other.title: The meal I eat most often
other.hook: I've eaten the same lunch most days this semester and I'm not sorry.
other.about: Simple, high-protein, repeatable food.
other.adapt: Show it being made, list the basics, close with 'simple, protein, consistent'.

other.title: Phone out of the room
other.hook: The most productive thing I did this week was leave my phone in another room.
other.about: A small focus habit that worked for you.
other.adapt: Say what changed, keep it understated.

other.title: The basics before anything else
other.hook: I don't have a morning routine, I have three things I don't skip.
other.about: Your real non-negotiables, without times or places.
other.adapt: List the three, one line each. No clock times.

other.title: A bad week, honestly
other.hook: This week didn't go to plan and I'm going to show it anyway.
other.about: Showing the process includes the off weeks.
other.adapt: Only real moments, dry humour welcome.

other.title: Small votes for who I want to be
other.hook: Every boring rep this week was a small vote for the person I'm trying to become.
other.about: Identity-based habits from your own life.
other.adapt: Your example, not a quote dump.

other.title: Comparing myself less
other.hook: I got happier with my progress the day I stopped comparing it to other people's highlights.
other.about: Comparison and calm, from your own experience.
other.adapt: Never name or mock other creators.

other.title: What a normal grocery run looks like
other.hook: My grocery list is boring on purpose.
other.about: The real food basics behind your training.
other.adapt: Show the items at home, not the store.

other.title: Studying like I train
other.hook: I started treating studying like a training program and my grades noticed.
other.about: Carrying gym structure into school work.
other.adapt: Keep it general, no school name, no grades you don't want to share.

other.title: What rest actually looks like for me
other.hook: Resting is a skill and I'm still bad at it.
other.about: Recovery outside the gym.
other.adapt: Honest and calm, no product plugs.

other.title: Resetting after a chaotic week
other.hook: When everything falls apart, I go back to the smallest version of my routine.
other.about: Minimum viable routine for hard weeks.
other.adapt: Say your smallest version in one line.

other.title: A full day of eating, no frills
other.hook: Here's everything I ate today, nothing hidden and nothing fancy.
other.about: Structured full-day-of-eating post.
other.adapt: Title line, one framing sentence, per-meal list, macros only if you have them.

other.title: Why I post the process
other.hook: I post the process because I forget how far I've come otherwise.
other.about: Why you document lifting, running, eating and trading.
other.adapt: Calm, one idea, no calls to action.

other.title: Running is humbling
other.hook: Lifting makes me feel strong and running immediately corrects that.
other.about: Mild self-pity humour about cardio.
other.adapt: One honest moment from a run, no route or place.

other.title: Discipline is mostly setup
other.hook: Most of my discipline is just making the right thing easier to do.
other.about: Environment design over willpower.
other.adapt: One real example from your room or bag, nothing that shows where you are.

other.title: Sunday prep
other.hook: My week is decided on Sunday, mostly in the kitchen.
other.about: Weekly meal prep and planning.
other.adapt: Show the prep, list the meals, keep it simple.

other.title: Waiting to feel motivated
other.hook: If I waited to feel motivated, I'd have trained about four times this year.
other.about: Acting before the feeling arrives.
other.adapt: Dry, honest, one closing line.

other.title: One hour without screens
other.hook: I tried one hour a day without screens and the first three days were rough.
other.about: A small experiment you actually ran.
other.adapt: Only if you really tried it; report honestly.

other.title: Progress is slower than the internet says
other.hook: Real progress is slower than the internet promised me, and that's okay.
other.about: Calm expectations, from your own timeline.
other.adapt: No body or money comparisons. Your own pace only.

other.title: Saying no to keep the routine
other.hook: Keeping a routine in college mostly means saying no to things I'd enjoy.
other.about: Trade-offs you make, honestly.
other.adapt: General, no names of people or places.

other.title: How I talk to myself after a bad day
other.hook: Being hard on myself never once made the next day better.
other.about: Self-compassion as a performance habit.
other.adapt: Your own words, calm, no lecture.

other.title: My Sunday review
other.hook: Every Sunday I ask myself three questions, and they're not about results.
other.about: A weekly reflection habit across lifting, trading and school.
other.adapt: Share the three questions, not private answers.

other.title: The basics I kept ignoring
other.hook: Drinking enough water fixed more of my bad days than any supplement.
other.about: Unglamorous basics you used to skip.
other.adapt: Your own experience, no health claims, no brands.

other.title: The busiest semester was the most consistent
other.hook: I was most consistent the semester I had the least free time.
other.about: Structure from constraints.
other.adapt: Keep it general; no school or schedule details.

other.title: Learning in public
other.hook: Posting while I'm still bad at things is the most useful habit I've built.
other.about: Why you share before you're good.
other.adapt: Calm, a little self-roast.

other.title: One thing a day
other.hook: On busy days I only promise myself one thing, and I keep it.
other.about: Minimum daily commitment.
other.adapt: Say your one thing for this week.

other.title: Cook once, eat four times
other.hook: I cook once and eat the same thing four times, and I've made peace with it.
other.about: Efficient meal prep.
other.adapt: Show the batch, list the macros only if you have them.

other.title: Quiet wins this month
other.hook: Nothing big happened this month, just a lot of small things I didn't skip.
other.about: Celebrating consistency, not milestones.
other.adapt: List two or three real small wins.

other.title: Managing energy, not time
other.hook: I stopped planning my days by hours and started planning them by energy.
other.about: How you match tasks to how you feel.
other.adapt: General, no clock times.

other.title: A note to me in a year
other.hook: I'm trying to be someone I'll thank in a year, and most days that's boring.
other.about: Long-term thinking in plain words.
other.adapt: Calm, one idea, end on a dry line.
